question: Why must the yogi keep returning attention to the seed-power?
premises: The seed is the luminous supreme power that is the cause of the universe.
Scripture identifies this source as the womb of all gods and powers, from which creation, withdrawal, and cognition unfold.
Attention to this seed means repeatedly placing the mind there.
inference: Therefore the yogi must continually fix attention on the supreme seed-power to remain established in that source.
uncertainties: The citation saṃharasṛṣṭi-pramāṇaprameya##ityādi is truncated in the token stream; its continuation is not recoverable from the listed tokens.
plain_english: The yogi must keep attention on the seed. That seed is the luminous supreme power, the cause of the whole universe. The cited scripture describes it as the source of all gods and powers, from which withdrawal, creation, and the whole field of knowing arise. So attention to the seed means placing the mind there again and again. When this is done, the yogi remains established in that source.
